issues.detail: The skill is a lookup reference with only a tiny ceil() formula and worked checks, so it offers no runnable code or step-by-step procedure for generating or validating a building model against the tables.

scenarios.name: mixed-use-restaurant-over-apartments-height-check
scenarios.rationale: Both classify R-2/A-2, use the S column at 5 stories/75 ft without a bonus, and flag Table 506.2; B stays close to the rubric and avoids stating unverified numbers, while A gives more detail but claims A-2 III-B S is 3 stories with 75 ft and asserts a 1-hr separation. It also conflicts with the rubric's 'each use meets its own limits' by treating the A-2 and R-2 limits as separate and wrongly picks separated use outright, but A's A-2 story limit of 3 may be inaccurate (A-2 III-B S is 3 stories is plausible) so the penalty is moderate.

scenarios.name: r2-egress-and-stair-width-check
scenarios.rationale: B hits all three rubric items cleanly (travel passes at 250 ft, stair width fails at 44 in, single exit fails with the 4-unit/3-story cap, and the unit doorway passes at ≤20 occupants and ≤125 ft common path), while A gets the main verdicts right but cites the wrong table for the single-exit exception (1006.3.4(2) instead of (1006.3.4(1))), hedges the common-path limit as 'at least 75 ft, I recall 125', and adds speculative extras.

scenarios.name: occupant-load-calculation-mixed-floors
scenarios.rationale: Both responses apply ceil(area/factor) with the correct Table 1004.5 factors and give 6, 21 and 84, and both say to round up; A adds a formula block and edition notes, while B adds a worked ceil() code block, so they are about equal on the rubric.
